name: Chu Shu-chen
bio: Chu Shu-chen is dated by Giles to the 9th century AD. Giles prints two of her poems, on early summer and on the spring of love.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Summer Begins
poems.author: Chu Shu-chen
poems.text:
What time the bamboo casts a deeper shade,
When birds fill up the afternoon with song,
When catkins vanish, and when pear-blooms fade, —
Then man is weary and the day is long.

poems.title: Love's Springtime
poems.author: Chu Shu-chen
poems.text:
Twin blossoms blooming on a single flower!
Then comes the jealous storm with shattering sound.
Oh could we always feel the
Spring-God's power,
No petals scattered on the moss-grown ground!
